key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells provide benefits beyond light trapping by improving wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and potentially mechanical stability.
engineering_relevance: Texture engineering is a practical design lever for boosting efficiency and device robustness in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Introduce nano- or micro-textured interfaces in the device stack
Use textures to improve perovskite-solution wetting and film formation
Leverage surface geometry to influence crystal growth, charge extraction, and stress behavior
evidence_signal: The paper is a review of recently reported texture-related effects, synthesizing qualitative findings rather than presenting new experimental measurements in the abstract.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on fabrication compatibility, uniformity, and the specific perovskite/device architecture, so process integration must be carefully controlled.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
